rows.grounds: genitive form of madraka; technical substance name in this recipe context, not glossed generically
accusative object; in this pharmacological recipe denotes the extracted fluid/substance to be taken
gerundive of grah; marks the prescribed substance as that which is to be appropriated/collected for use
genitive of lakṣaṇa; technical term here likely denotes a specified type/substance rather than a general 'mark'
genitive of makara; technical substance/name in this recipe sequence, load-bearing in situ

items.question: On what basis must the juice of madraka be taken together with the specified substances of lakṣaṇa and makara in this prescribed recipe?
premises: The juice of madraka is designated as the substance to be taken.
The substances of lakṣaṇa and makara are specified as co-requisites in the prescription.
The coordinating particle links all three items into a single required combination.
items.inference: Within this recipe sequence, the madraka juice is to be taken in conjunction with the specified lakṣaṇa and makara substances, not as a standalone item.
uncertainties: The precise technical referents of madraka, lakṣaṇa, and makara remain context-bound to this tantra's pharmacological usage.
It is not determinable from this verse alone whether 'grāhyaṃ' marks collection, ingestion, or ritual appropriation.
items.plain_english: The juice of madraka is to be taken, and likewise that of lakṣaṇa and of makara.
